cohort: The study included 1350 pregnant women from diverse, multiethnic populations in three tertiary care hospitals and one intermediate obstetrics care facility in Sri Lanka.
finding: NCDs are highly prevalent among pregnant women in Sri Lanka and are significantly associated with adverse maternal and fetal outcomes, including preterm birth, neonatal sepsis, hypoglycaemia, postpartum haemorrhage, and placental abruption.
cross-section timing: Data was collected over 3 months from discharged bed head tickets of the postnatal obstetric wards.
